hook.text: Iceland, the Azores, and Réunion all rose from the sea—born of volcanic eruptions on the ocean floor.

buildup.text: Volcanic islands form when submarine volcanoes erupt enough material to break the ocean surface.

discovery.text: Island arcs (like Japan and the Philippines) form above subduction zones—in curved chains.

twist.text: Hot-spot islands like Hawaii slowly sink beneath the waves after the plate carries them off the magma source.

climax.text: Coral atolls are the final stage—a reef ring marking where a volcanic island once stood.

punchline.text: Volcanic islands are born from the sea—and eventually return to it.

quiz.question: What is an atoll?
options: A coral reef ring where a volcanic island once existed
